'''Braden Lee Smith''' (born July 25, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Noblesville Boom]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]]. He is the [[NCAA Division I]] men's basketball all-time career assist leader.

==Early life and high school career==
Smith was born in [[Russellville, Arkansas]], and moved with his family to [[Westfield, Indiana]], at age four.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4100268/2023/01/18/purdue-braden-smith-freshman-recruiting/|title=Purdue's Braden Smith was the No. 196 freshman recruit. Now he's the Boilers' floor general|first=Brian|last=Hamilton|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=January 18, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2023}}</ref> He attended [[Westfield High School (Westfield, Indiana)|Westfield High School]] and made the varsity basketball team as a freshman. Smith was named first-team All-[[Hoosier Crossroads Conference]] (HCC) after he averaged 18.5 points, 5.4 rebounds, 4.7 assists, and 1.5 steals per game during his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/07/14/indiana-high-school-basketball-recruiting-braden-smith-javon-small-jalen-clark/5423364002/|title=Catching up with Braden Smith, Javon Small and Jalen Clark |work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=July 14, 2020|access-date=November 10, 2022}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 22.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, 5.4 assists, and 2.7 steals per game and was named high-honorable mention All-State in addition to repeating as a first team All-HCC selection.<ref name=mom>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/12/28/purdue-basketball-recruit-braden-smith-stars-westfield-boys-mom-ginny-smith-coaches-girls-shamrocks/9021399002/|title=Purdue recruit Braden Smith leads Westfield boys, mom coaches girls|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=December 28, 2021|access-date=November 10, 2022}}</ref> Smith was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] after averaging 18.3 points, six rebounds, six assists, and 1.9 steals while leading Westfield to their first sectional championship.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2022/06/11/purdue-basketball-indiana-mr-basketball-braden-smith-sits-idle-with-big-picture-in-mind-all-stars/7571126001/|title=Purdue basketball: Indiana Mr. Basketball Braden Smith sits idle with big picture in mind|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|date=June 11, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/04/02/indiana-mr-basketball-2022-winner-braden-smith-westfield-purdue-recruit/7215882001/|title=Too small? It only fueled fire within Braden Smith, who is 2022 Indiana Mr. Basketball.|first=Kyle|last=Neddenriep |work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=April 2, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}}</ref> He also missed several weeks due to a foot injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/01/24/westfield-high-school-purdue-basketball-recruit-braden-smith-injury-indiana-mr-basketball-2022/9202066002/|title=Westfield star, Purdue recruit Braden Smith to miss at least 3-4 weeks|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=January 24, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}}</ref>

Smith was rated a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] over offers from [[Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball|Appalachian State]], [[Belmont Bruins men's basketball|Belmont]], [[Montana Grizzlies basketball|Montana]], [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas]], and [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2021/04/29/purdue-basketball-recruiting-westfield-guard-braden-smith-commits/4887446001/|title=Purdue basketball recruiting: Westfield guard Braden Smith commits|first=Mike |last=Carmin|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|date=April 29, 2021|access-date=November 10, 2022}}</ref> At the time of his commitment Purdue was his only major-conference offer, but he had recently begun to receive interest from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/04/29/purdue-basketball-westfield-highs-braden-smith-commits-boilermakers/4886125001/|title=Westfield High's Braden Smith commits to play at Purdue|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=April 29, 2021|access-date=November 10, 2022}}</ref>

|url=https://purdue.rivals.com/news/braden-smith-the-next-purdue-point-guard?|title=Braden Smith: The Next Purdue Point Guard|first=Casey|last=Bartley|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=November 11, 2022|access-date=November 17, 2022}}</ref> In his college debut in the season opener against [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee]], he scored seven points with four rebounds, four assists and set a freshman record with seven steals in an 84–57 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2022/11/09/milwaukee-at-purdue-braden-smiths-debut-impressive-but-not-a-surprise/69627765007/|title=Milwaukee at Purdue: Braden Mr. Basketball Braden Smith takes over|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=November 16, 2022 |access-date=November 16, 2022}}</ref> Smith was named the [[Big Ten Conference]] Freshman of the Week after scoring 20 points with three assists and two rebounds in a 75–70 win over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/purdue-guard-braden-smith-named-big-ten-basketball-freshman-of-the-week|title=Purdue guard Braden Smith scored 20 points in a 75-70 victory over Marquette last week inside Mackey Arena. His performance pushed the Boilermakers to 3-0 and earned him Big Ten Freshman of the Week honors.|first=D.J.|last=Fezler|website=[[SI.com]]|date=November 21, 2022|access-date=November 22, 2022}}</ref> He started all 35 of the Boilermakers' games and was named to the [[Big Ten Conference]] All-Freshman team after averaging 9.7 points, 4.4 assists, 4.2 rebounds, and 1.2 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/2023/11/03/purdue-basketball-on-the-rebound-zach-edey-daily-cover|title=Purdue Men's Basketball Is Ready for Redemption|first=Kevin|last=Sweeney|website=[[SI.com]]|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref> Purdue won the [[2022–23 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2022–23 Big Ten Conference men's basketball regular season]] championship (the school's 25th) as well as the [[2023 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/news/2023/3/12/general-purdue-wins-2023-big-ten-mens-basketball-championship.aspx|title=Purdue Wins 2023 Big Ten Men's Basketball Championship|access-date=March 17, 2023|date=March 12, 2023|website=BigTen.org|archive-date=March 17, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230317221812/https://bigten.org/news/2023/3/12/general-purdue-wins-2023-big-ten-mens-basketball-championship.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/news/2023/2/26/general-purdue-clinches-share-of-big-ten-mens-basketball-title.aspx|title=Purdue Clinches Share of Big Ten Men's Basketball Title|access-date=March 17, 2023|date=February 26, 2023|website=BigTen.org|archive-date=March 17, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230317223402/https://bigten.org/news/2023/2/26/general-purdue-clinches-share-of-big-ten-mens-basketball-title.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

tournament]] first-round game in Columbus, the [[2023 Fairleigh Dickinson vs. Purdue men's basketball game|biggest upset in tournament history]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/why-16-seed-fairleigh-dickinson-over-1-seed-purdue-is-the-biggest-upset-in-ncaa-tournament-history/|title=Why 16-seed Fairleigh Dickinson over 1-seed Purdue is the biggest upset in NCAA Tournament history|accessdate=March 18, 2023|date=March 17, 2023|work=[[CBS Sports]]|author=Patterson, Chip|archive-date=March 18, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318044401/https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/why-16-seed-fairleigh-dickinson-over-1-seed-purdue-is-the-biggest-upset-in-ncaa-tournament-history/|url-status=live}}</ref> The backcourt pair of Smith and Loyer each started a school freshman record 35 games and finished the season as Purdue's 2nd highest scoring freshman duo (Loyer 384/Smith 340, 724 total) behind [[Robbie Hummel]] and [[E'Twaun Moore]] (813, 2008).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://purduesports.com/documents/2023/3/14/GAME35_Purdue_Game_Notes.pdf|title=Purdue Boilermakers: 2022–23 Boilerball Game Notes: Game 35 // Fairleigh Dickinson Or Texas Southern // NCAA Tournament First Round // March 17, 2023|accessdate=March 18, 2023|date=March 14, 2023|publisher=[[Purdue ===Sophomore season===
Smith returned as the starting Point Guard in his sophomore season. On March 5, in a win against Illinois, Smith broke the Purdue single season assist record with his 208th assist.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Justin|last1=Rudolph|url=https://www.on3.com/college/purdue-boilermakers/news/purdue-guard-braden-smith-sets-program-record-for-most-assists-in-a-season-vs-illinois-zach-edey/|title=Purdue guard Braden Smith sets program record for most assists in a season vs Illinois|work=on3|date=March 5, 2024|access-date=March 19, 2024}}</ref> The previous record, set by Bruce Parkinson, had stood since 1975.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}} Purdue clinched a second consecutive [[2023–24 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten regular season Championship]] with a March 2 victory over [[2023–24 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] as Smith contributed 23 points and 9 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401600418|title=Edey leads No. 2 Purdue past Michigan State 80-74 to clinch share of 2nd straight Big Ten title|accessdate=February 21, 2026|date=March 2, 2024|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> On March 12, Smith was named first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/news/2024/3/12/general-big-ten-announces-2024-mens-basketball-postseason-honors.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312183111/https://bigten.org/news/2024/3/12/general-big-ten-announces-2024-mens-basketball-postseason-honors.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 12, 2024|title=Big Ten Announces 2024 Men's Basketball Postseason Honors|website=[[Big Ten Conference]]|date=March 12, 2024|access-date=March 19, 2024}}</ref> By the end of the season Braden Smith led the nation in total assists and was named an Honorable Mention All-American.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}} In the Sweet Sixteen vs Gonzaga, Braden Smith had 14 points and 15 assists in Purdue's victory. Smith's 15 assists were the most by one player in a tournament game in Purdue history as well as in Big Ten history (tied with [[Mike Smith (basketball, born 1997)|Mike Smith]]).{{citation needed|date=March 2026}}  In the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|National Championship game]], Smith broke the Big Ten single season assist record with his 292nd assist narrowly passing the previous record holder, Cassius Winston, by one assist.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}}

===Junior season===
Smith was a consensus [[2025 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2025 NCAA Men's Basketball All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Associated Press All-America Team |url=https://apnews.com/article/ap-allamerica-mens-basketball-teams-3c18f2c7fe8e56ff1c912df512b70836|date=March 18, 2025|work=AP News}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|title= USBWA unveils 2024-25 Men's All-America Team |date=March 19, 2025|url= https://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2025/03/19/usbwa-unveils-2024-25-mens-all-america-team |work=[[United States Basketball Writers Association]]|access-date=March 19, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|title= NABC Division I All-America Teams Announced |date=March 19, 2025|url= https://nabc.com/nabc_releases/2025/nabc-division-i-all-america-teams-announced-2/ |work=[[National Association of Basketball Coaches]]|access-date=March 19, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=DeCourcy|first=Mike|title= The Sporting News 2024-25 College Basketball All-America Team |date=March 12, 2025|url= https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/sporting-news-2024-25-college-basketball-all-america-team/bd32682b993fdb8a1014ba54 |work=[[The Sporting News]]|access-date=March 17, 2024}}</ref>

===Senior season===
On his March 7 [[senior day]] against [[2025–26 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]], Smith and [[Fletcher Loyer]] tied the school record for games played by [[Dakota Mathias]] (141).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/fletcher-loyer-makes-purdue-history-final-game-mackey-arena-three-point-leader|title=Fletcher Loyer Makes Purdue History in Final Game at Mackey Arena|accessdate=March 23, 2026|date=March 7, 2026|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|author=Schutte, Dustin}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://purduesports.com/news/2026/03/7/wisconsin-spoils-15-purdue-senior-day-97-93|title=Wisconsin Spoils #15 Purdue Senior Day, 97-93|accessdate=March 23, 2026|date=March 7, 2026|publisher=[[Purdue Boilermakers]]}}</ref> After losing 4 of its 6 final regular season games, Purdue won 4 in 4 days to capture the [[2026 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] with a victory over [[2025–26 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] on March 15. Smith contributed 14 points, 11 assists and 3 steals in the victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401851388|title=Cluff and Kaufman-Renn power No. 18 Purdue past No. 3 Michigan 80-72 in Big Ten final|accessdate=March 23, 2026|date=March 15, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> At the [[2026 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]], Smith established the [[Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] single-game (16), single tournament (46) and career (96) assists record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7120656/2026/03/15/purdue-michigan-big-ten-championship-basketball-score-result/|title=Braden Smith, Purdue cap brilliant run through Big Ten tourney with upset of Michigan|accessdate=March 18, 2026|date=March 15, 2026|work=[[The Athletic]]|publisher=[[The New York Times]]|author=Dochterman, Scott}}</ref> On March 20, Smith broke the [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career assists leaders|NCAA Division I men's basketball all-time career assist record]], previously held for 33 years by [[Bobby Hurley]] (1076), against the [[2025–26 Queens Royals men's basketball team|Queens Royals]] in the first round of the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2026 NCAA Tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401856519|title=Purdue's Smith sets Division I career assists record in rout of Queens University in NCAA Tournament|accessdate=March 23, 2026|date=March 20, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

Smith finished his Purdue career with 1,103 assists (NCAA record), 5,067 minutes minutes played (NCAA four-year career record, surpassing [[Lionel Simmons]] of [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]] 5,045; 1987–90), 1,932 points (8th in Purdue history), 249 steals (3rd in Purdue history) and 673 rebounds (17th in Purdue history). His 345 senior season assists the fifth in NCAA history. His senior class with Loyer and [[Trey Kaufman-Renn]] finished with a school record four-season win total of 117 (Only surpassed in Big Ten history by 2013 Ohio State - 123; 2014 Ohio State - 119).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://purduesports.com/news/2026/03/28/mbb-recap-purdue-arizona|title=No. 2 Purdue Falls to No. 1 Arizona to End Tournament Run|accessdate=March 30, 2026|date=March 28, 2026|publisher=[[Purdue Boilermakers]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 24, 2026, Smith was selected with the 38th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]] by the [[Chicago Bulls]] but was subsequently traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] on draft night in exchange for [[Kam Jones]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 24, 2026 |title=Pacers trade for No. 38 overall pick Braden Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/news/pacers-bulls-trade-second-round-2026-nba-draft |access-date=June 24, 2025 |website=[[National Basketball Association|NBA.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Poe |first=Julia |title=NBA draft: Chicago Bulls trade their two 2nd-round picks and reportedly acquire Kam Jones from Indiana Pacers
|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/06/24/chicago-bulls-nba-draft-kam-jones/ |work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=June 24, 2026}}</ref> The Pacers signed him to a [[Two-way contract|two-way contract]], splitting his availability between the Indiana Pacers and the [[NBA G League|G League]]'s [[Noblesville Boom]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-25 |title=Pacers to Sign Braden Smith to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/onsi/pacers-to-sign-braden-smith-to-two-way-contract-01kvye4g6gr8 |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Indiana Pacers On SI |language=en-US}}</ref>

Smith majored in [[Organizational Leadership]] at [[Purdue University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Braden Smith - Men's Basketball |url=https://purduesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/braden-smith/13077 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=Purdue Boilermakers |language=en}}</ref>
